name: Ambient track from variation sets: give each voice (texture, pad, melody) lettered variations (filter low/mid/high, modulation depth), chain them along a presence/focus map, and plan frequency slots so layers never fight
goal: Build an evolving ambient track from three voices (a looping sample texture, a slow paraphonic pad, a floating repetitive melody) without a muddy, aimless wall of reverb. (1) Start with one sound and one reverb and develop a set of variations (A, B, C...) using filters (driven low, wide mid, thin high) and attenuated slow modulation. (2) Chain variations within each voice to tell a story, with slow automatic modulation adding depth but not changing the voice's role. (3) Draw a presence/focus map (focus, not volume) for the three voices across the track and assign a variation per section. (4) Match it to a low/mid/high frequency-slot map and resolve clashes by switching variations or EQ. Delta vs arrangement-ambient cluster: the per-voice variation set and focus-not-volume map tied to a frequency-slot plan.

source.title: Learn to make ambient music in 4 simple steps

prerequisites: A synth or modular with 2 oscillators, mixer, high-pass + low-pass filters, a decay envelope and a step sequencer (two sequences of different lengths)
A sampler/looper with a band-pass filter
LFOs / smooth random sources with attenuators (or mod-matrix depth controls)
One reverb; a mixer with 3-band EQ per channel

inputs.name: pad_notes
inputs.description: Two step sequences, 3 and 4 steps long, for the pad's two oscillators

outputs.name: variation_sheet
outputs.description: Per voice: lettered variations with filter/mod settings

outputs.name: focus_map
outputs.description: Section-by-section focus and assigned variation per voice

constraints: Use a single reverb while exploring; build depth from the core sounds rather than effects.
Every modulation goes through an attenuator so variations blend smoothly.
Dropped for Matt: the transcript's smooth-random modulation of the sample playback speed (pitch wobble). Move the texture with filter cutoff/band-pass only; keep pitch steady.
Slow modulation is timbre-only (wave shape, filter, FM depth via VCA) and subtle; it adds depth but must not move the voice to a different role or register.
If the track has drums, they enter early (~8 counts / ~12 s); only pad/texture before that (Matt's preference).
Ableton/MIDI-friendly: device names map to stock Live devices or generic modules; patterns are plain MIDI clips.

Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with Ableton, Reason, Bitwig, Soundtoys, FabFilter, Eventide or any vendor. Map product devices to generic modules (sampler, noise osc, filter, envelope, LFO, EQ, saturator, compressor, delay, reverb) in any DAW, hardware or Web Audio.
Steady pitch: no random pitch wobble or randomised notes; no rapid clicking textures (Matt's preference).

steps.action: Pick one inspiring sound and stay with it; use only one reverb. Aim for a sound with depth and a set of lettered variations (A, B, C...).

Pad: two oscillators into a mixer, then high-pass and low-pass filters. Feed the oscillators two different step sequences (3 steps and 4 steps) for a paraphonic polymetric pad; a gate into a decay envelope opens the low-pass. Make filter variations: driven low, wide mid-range, thin high.
steps.expect: Three pad variations from filters alone

steps.action: Add modulation variations through attenuators: slow smooth random on the wavetable shape of one oscillator (works best on the low variation); an LFO through a VCA into the FM input of the other (works best on mid and high variations).
steps.expect: Pad can morph smoothly between variations

steps.action: Melody voice: single oscillator, high-pass + low-pass, sequencer and decay envelope, with attenuated LFOs on filter spread and wave shape. Texture voice: looping sample through a band-pass filter. Make front/back variations of each (push back with the filter, bring forward with modulation; texture from deep modulated rumble to bright crispy top).
steps.expect: Each voice can move between foreground and background

steps.action: Draw a presence/focus map (focus, not volume) for the three voices. Example from the transcript: open on a present sample texture (solo intro carrying the track), pad enters and pushes the texture back, both step back when the melody enters, melody in focus for a while, pad and noise come back up, then all calm to a slow outro.
steps.expect: Section plan showing which voice is in focus when

steps.action: Assign a variation to each section: a deep, heavily modulated texture variation to carry the intro, a background variation while the pad is central, a bright low-cut noise variation when the melody is focal. A focal sound needs depth and weight; a background sound should be pleasant without effort.
steps.expect: Every section has a defined variation per voice

steps.action: Make a frequency-slot map (low / mid / high) beside the focus map. When two voices want the same slot (dark rumbling texture + dark pad), either use a brighter pad variation with little low end, make the texture thin and high from the start, or cut the texture's lows before/while the low pad enters. Use a mixer's 3-band EQ as a playable variation control, not set-and-forget.
steps.expect: Layers sit in separate slots; no mud when voices overlap

steps.action: Perform/automate the main evolution by hand along the focus map, letting the slow automatic modulation keep background voices alive; render.
steps.expect: Evolving track that tells a story

verification: Each voice has >= 3 named variations recorded on the variation sheet.
Focus map assigns exactly one focal voice per section.
Spectral check: in overlapping sections the two lowest voices do not share the same dominant band (e.g. low-band energy owned by one voice at a time).
